newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA DECLARES OIL FORCE MAJEURE IN CURACAO.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA DECLARES OIL FORCE MAJEURE IN CURACAO.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) declared force majeure on all the output from its fire-striken Curacao oil refinery in the Caribbean, a Venezuelan trader said.

The trader said no shipments of refined products had yet been cancelled, but that cancellations were possible after a fire disabled the refinery's main 180,000 barrel-per-day crude distillation unit on Thursday last week.
"The force majeure says that we could have problems in supplying the products for reasons beyond our control and we are making our best efforts to solve the problem," the trader said.
The fire cut refinery throughput from 190,000 barrels per day (bpd) to about 60,000 bpd on Thursday, but by Friday output was already up to 105,000 bpd.
Refinery managers said they hoped to achieve 170,000 bpd by August 22.
They said they would import naphtha and jet fuel to meet contractual requirements, but reduced gasoline production at PDVSA's Cardon refinery confused the situation further.

The trader said one 230,000 barrel cargo of premium unleaded gasoline had already been cancelled from Cardon's August programme, and more were at risk. He did not know if any cargoes would be cancelled from the Curacao plant.
The 300,000 bpd Cardon refinery normally exports five or six cargoes of premium unleaded gasoline per month, but the problems mean that the refinery cannot produce high-octane products.
Cardon is a major supplier of refined products to the U.S. market, while Curacao supplies mostly Caribbean markets.
